review_reference: Owner decision in chat by D-Eminence. 0106: seeds the OCR worker's workload account (subject hid:staging:ocr-worker, source_system hid-workload, no email, no password) and gives it the platform ocr_worker role (0013; grants only ocr.job.process) outside auth.admin_change_platform_role, which refuses that role (0064), as 0105 did for the document scanner. Numbered 0106 as the next free number after production's 0105 (verify-release-contract refuses a gap), superseding the 2026-11-03 decision 33(6) allocation of 0106 to the support check. Signed: the owner approved this release in chat on 2026-11-04 (about 23:45 UTC) with "approve 0106".
evidence: Single migration 0106_ocr_worker_account.sql. WHY: since the OCR worker started, production's Postgres logs show ocr.claim_worker_job(text,integer) (0014, replaced by 0105) refused about 4 times a minute with 42501 Authorized OCR workload context is required (4 Nov 21:40 UTC): the worker sets app.actor_subject from OCR_WORKER_SUBJECT, and no auth.accounts row holding the platform ocr_worker role exists for any subject. No migration, release step or admin command on any branch creates one. WHAT IT DOES: inserts exactly two rows, the account 0c4e0106-0106-4000-8000-000000000001 (subject hid:staging:ocr-worker, display name OCR worker, active) and its role row 0c4e0106-0106-4000-8000-000000000002 (platform ocr_worker, granted_by null, grant_reason naming migration 0106), ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING followed by exact-row checks. No function, policy, table, grant or runtime-grants.sql change; no patient data read or written; no audit row (a dry run would consume audit.events' sequence). Preconditions (55000 or 42501, nothing applied): 0105 applied (ehr.resolve_document_scan_target is the marker); not already applied (else 0106: already applied); auth.account_id_for_subject md5 4678770cf6a210034740f09422fdfbaa and auth.account_has_active_role md5 a3310b48da6ff8bcd3ecb9d7dbef900a (the pins 0105 uses); ocr.claim_worker_job still calls both for ocr_worker; the columns written; ocr_worker active and granting exactly ocr.job.process; the applier may read and insert both tables and execute both helpers. A post-check runs the worker's own test for the new subject. TERRAFORM: OCR_WORKER_SUBJECT is already hid:staging:ocr-worker in production (hid-system#179 on dev, applied 2026-11-04 in apply 3; ocr-worker task definition :25, recorded in the release index by #182), so the running worker claims as soon as this release applies 0106; until then it answers 42501 as before. The document scanner is live in write mode (apply 3), so a claim takes jobs whose document's latest scan is clean (0105). Kill switch, no release needed: revoke the role row or set the account's status to disabled. ORDER: verify-release-contract refuses a gap in migration prefixes, so this file takes 0106, the next free number after production's 0105 (renumbered from a later draft number; only its number, messages and fixed ids changed); the planned support check moves to a later number. PROOF on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster run as pgrun (never a real database): a 0105 database built by f11c9ec9's runner and bootstrapped with its runtime-grants.sql reproduces production's refusal (42501 for hid:staging:ocr-api as hid_ocr_worker). UPGRADE: plan 1 pending; dry run rolled back with no account or role row; apply; then 0 pending, the runner again 0 pending, the file again answers 0106: already applied; 1236 non-owner grants before and after, identical md5 (e82d05f38f5e567cc73bd15941f85d86), the bootstrap and --verify-only pass and change none. FRESH install of all 107 files (dry run leaves no ledger table, apply, re-run 0 pending, already applied; same 1236 grants) (renumbered file re-proved on PostgreSQL 16.15: upgrade from 0105, re-run, fresh install, claims, all 80 suites on both). The MIGRATION_TARGET=rds fresh install, re-owned applier, negative copies and lock measurements below were run on this file before its renumbering, when only its number, messages and fixed ids differed. As hid_ocr_worker with the worker's session: hid:staging:ocr-worker claims (0 rows with no job; the new suite claims its fixture job and writes one ocr.worker.claim audit row naming the worker account), while hid:staging:ocr-api, a random hid:staging:<uuid>, an empty subject, the scanner's subject and a near-miss subject still get 42501, as do the seeded subject with its role revoked or its account disabled. A NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner of every object applies it; a login without privileges is refused (42501) with nothing applied. Negative copies each refuse with nothing applied: 0105 missing, the subject held by another account, the seeded id present, an extra ocr_worker permission, ocr_worker inactive, a changed helper body, a claim that no longer checks ocr_worker, a changed column. Locks before commit: ROW EXCLUSIVE on auth.accounts and auth.account_roles, ROW SHARE on auth.accounts and auth.roles, ACCESS SHARE on those and auth.role_permissions and identity.sealed_demo_members; nothing on ocr.jobs, ehr.documents or audit.events. All 80 database suites pass on the upgraded, fresh and rds databases (79 existing and the new test/database/ocr-worker-account.integration.sql), which also passes on the re-owned database. verify-migration-ledger passes 107 migrations (0106 last).
